title: ALMA reveals a dust-obscured galaxy merger at cosmic noon
question: Determine the baryonic properties (SFR, stellar, molecular gas and dust masses) of the two galaxies in a serendipitously discovered, dust-obscured merger at z=1.17

data.angular_resolution: CO(2-1) beam 1.5'' x 1.3''; CO(5-4) and Band 6 continuum beam 0.8'' x 0.7''
data.sensitivity: CO(2-1): 0.82 mJy/beam per 75 km/s channel; CO(5-4): 0.81 mJy/beam per 75 km/s channel; continuum: 0.23 mJy/beam

evidence.loc: 3.1 Identification of the dusty galaxy merger
evidence.quote: we conclude that we are witnessing two galaxies at $z=1.17223 \pm 0.00037$ ((cite: Valentino2020)) merging.

evidence.loc: 3.4 The molecular gas masses from the CO(2-1) emission
evidence.quote: the mean and standard deviation measured for a sample of $z=1-3$ DSFGs in (cite: Harrington2021)

evidence.loc: 3.4 The molecular gas masses from the CO(2-1) emission
evidence.quote: assuming a ratio of 0.85 between the CO(2–1) and CO(1–0) luminosities ((cite: Carilli2013))

recipe.goal: Image CO(2-1), CO(5-4) and Band 6 continuum from calibrated visibilities
recipe.method: uv-plane continuum subtraction, tclean imaging with natural weighting in 75 km/s channels, moment-0 maps integrated over a selected velocity range

recipe.goal: Identify the merger by comparing ALMA with HST, VISTA, Spitzer and VLA
recipe.method: Compare the morphology and peaks of CO and dust continuum with ancillary images; North is the VLA and ALMA peak with no HST emission, South is the HST galaxy

recipe.goal: Image the velocity offset between negative and positive velocity peaks
recipe.method: Moment-0 maps integrated separately over negative and positive velocities for CO(2-1) and CO(5-4)

recipe.goal: Deblend and measure CO(2-1), CO(5-4) and continuum fluxes of North and South
recipe.method: Flux of North measured within a single-beam element centred on it; South taken as 3 sigma upper limit from the remaining emission inside the CO(2-1) 3 sigma contours; same procedure for CO(5-4) and continuum
key_parameters: Flux error is the standard deviation of the intensity map with the merger emission within 2'' masked
assumptions: All gas not associated with North belongs to South

recipe.goal: Convert CO(2-1) flux to line luminosity and molecular gas mass
recipe.method: Flux to L'CO(2-1) with the standard equation, then to CO(1-0) with a ratio of 0.85, then to M_H2 with alpha_CO
assumptions: alpha_CO from z=1-3 DSFGs; r21 = 0.85; Lambda-CDM H0 = 70, Om = 0.3, OL = 0.7

recipe.method: Ratio of the deblended CO(5-4) and CO(2-1) fluxes of North, compared with literature samples; South omitted because only upper limits

recipe.goal: Deblend and extract multi-band photometry for North and South
recipe.method: PhoEBO deblending using radio and NIR high-resolution priors with PSF matching, followed by fixed-aperture photometry with Photutils; 0.15 mag added in quadrature to uncertainties
key_parameters: Aperture diameter 4'' fixed; background from a two arcsec-wide annulus

recipe.goal: SED fitting for stellar mass, dust mass and SFR
recipe.method: Separate MAGPHYS SED fits of North and South with the redshift fixed, including the ALMA Band 6 continuum; SFR cross-checked with VLA 3 GHz

recipe.goal: Compare with main-sequence scaling relations (SFR, depletion time, gas fraction)
recipe.method: Compare North and South SFR with the Speagle main sequence, and depletion time and gas fraction with the Tacconi 2018 relations at z=1.17
